summary.headline: Orders and revenue both landed behind target this week, and year-to-date revenue stays behind target with the recent pace short of what the rest of 2026 requires.

points.what: Orders reached 99.6% of target and revenue reached 96.7% of target this week, both landing behind target.
points.so_what: Both key weekly measures missed target despite week-over-week growth, showing this week's gains were not enough to close the gap.

points.what: Orders grew 61.0% year on year and revenue grew 54.3% year on year, both below the 75% growth rate the 2026 targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth running below the pace the targets assume is consistent with a growing week still landing behind target.

points.what: Orders were flagged as notable, with this week's level sitting outside the normal 8-week range.
points.so_what: This level should not be read as part of a normal growth trend for orders.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 94.4% of target, behind, and the current 8-week revenue run-rate of $53,042 is well below the $75,259 weekly pace needed for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: The required weekly revenue run-rate to hit the full-year target is $75,259, well above the current 8-week run-rate of $53,042.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Jan 12 rose to 9.8%, up 0.1pp week on week and up 1.1pp year on year, both bad-direction moves.
points.so_what: Returns are trending in the wrong direction on both comparisons, a risk to revenue quality.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 2.1pp year on year to 16.5%, even though it fell 0.2pp week on week.
points.so_what: The year-on-year rise in cancellations is a risk sitting behind the small week-over-week improvement.

points.what: Orders were 99.6% of target and revenue was 96.7% of target this week, both status behind.
points.so_what: The week finished behind target on both core measures despite growth week over week.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 94.4% of target, behind, with $498,187 still needed against the full-quarter target over the remaining 8 weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter needs stronger weekly revenue than achieved so far to close the gap to target.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 94.4% of target, behind, and closing the full-year gap requires a weekly run-rate of $75,259 versus the current 8-week run-rate of $53,042.
points.so_what: The recent pace falls well short of what the rest of the year requires to hit the full-year target.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 20.0% week on week, contributing +30 orders, the largest positive contributor to the week's order change.
points.so_what: Order growth this week was concentrated in EMEA rather than spread across regions.

points.what: APAC orders fell 9.4% week on week, contributing -32 orders, the largest negative contributor.
points.so_what: APAC's decline nearly offset EMEA's gain, holding total order growth to a small net change.

points.what: Organic orders rose 23.4% week on week, contributing +25 orders, the largest positive contributor among traffic sources, while Search, the largest channel by share, fell 2.7% week on week and contributed -15 orders.
points.so_what: The week's order growth came from a smaller channel rather than the dominant Search channel, which pulled the total down.

points.what: AOV rose 0.8% week on week to $85.64 but fell 1.8% year on year.
points.so_what: Baskets are smaller than a year ago even as they ticked up week over week, meaning revenue growth is coming more from order volume than basket size.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 0.2pp week on week to 16.5% but rose 2.1pp year on year.
points.so_what: The year-on-year direction remains bad even though the week-over-week move improved slightly.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Jan 12 was 9.8%, up 0.1pp week on week and up 1.1pp year on year.
points.so_what: Returns are moving in the bad direction on both comparisons.

points.what: New signups rose 14.2% year on year, well below orders' 61.0% year-on-year growth.
points.so_what: Signup growth is lagging the pace of order growth this year, a gap worth watching alongside the otherwise strong order trend.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
